upcoming_dates: 2026-09-30 | dividend | Cash dividend of US$0.28 per common share payment date | https://investors.pagbank.com/investor-services/dividends/ | primary
product: Merchant acquiring plus embedded financial services. Merchants adopt PagBank POS/card acceptance, then its digital account: Q2 2026 Cash-In R$97.0bn (+23.3% y/y), deposits R$42.8bn (+15.1%), and credit R$5.1bn (+30.7%) - working capital, payroll loans, card receivables - plus merchant prepayment R$47.3bn. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
demand: Mostly mix, some volume. Q2 2026 TPV grew 3.0% y/y (volume) yet Payments revenue fell 4.7% y/y (price/mix), while Banking revenue rose 28.9% y/y and reached 24% of revenue ex-ITC. Total revenue ex-ITC +1.7% y/y. Growth is Banking-mix-driven, not acquiring pricing power. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
pricing_power: Rising unsecured credit losses: Q2 2026 allowances R$70m vs R$28m and NPL90 3.4% vs 2.5%; higher SELIC/funding (financial costs R$1,274m); tax: statutory rate 34% to 37% and Law 224/2025 incentive cut from 2026-04-01; elevated marketing (World Cup sponsorship) and admin expenses. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
competition: Not Chinese; the closest low-cost substitute is Brazil Pix, free instant payments that undercut card MDR, plus Nubank, Mercado Pago, Stone and Cielo. PagBank itself pushes Pix/cash-in, R$97.0bn up 23.3% y/y, so the substitute is already at scale. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
market_strategy: CEO Carlos Mauad, 2026-08-11: 2029 ambition is a R$25 billion Credit Portfolio, gross profit CAGR of approximately 10% and EPS CAGR above 16% between 2025 and 2029. On 2026-09-01 the company said it expects to distribute at least R$2.0bn dividends in 2027-2028 and a US$150m buyback. (SEC 6-K)
bull: Q2 2026 6-K: Banking revenue +28.9% y/y, deposits R$42.8bn +15.1%, credit R$5.1bn +30.7%; third buyback completed, US$0.28 dividend due 2026-09-30, and 2026-09-01 pledge of R$2.0bn dividends for 2027-2028 plus US$150m buyback.
bear: Q2 2026 6-K: allowances R$70m vs R$28m, NPL90 3.4% vs 2.5%, unsecured +142.7%, active clients -3.3%, Payments revenue -4.7% y/y, tax 34% to 37%; founder-chairman resigned 2026-08-21; 90d net raises -1, median target change -10.7%.
falsifier: Q3 2026 6-K showing NPL90 above 4.0% or quarterly credit-loss allowances above R$70m while unsecured lending keeps rising.
web_what_changed_30_90d: 2026-09-01 SEC 6-K: dividend target at least R$2.0bn for 2027-2028 plus 4th buyback up to US$150m. 2026-09-02 Goldman Sachs held Hold/$10. 2026-08-11 Q2 results: non-GAAP net income R$576m, TPV +3.0% y/y, US$0.28 dividend due 2026-09-30. 2026-08-21 founder-chairman Luis Frias resigned; Maria Judith de Brito chairman. Analysts cut: BofA 07-15, UBS 07-17, Jefferies 07-23, Morgan Stanley 08-12.
web_true_now_not_modelled: Credit risk and tax are re-pricing: Q2 2026 credit-loss allowance jumped to R$70m from R$28m y/y, NPL90 rose to 3.4% from 2.5%, unsecured/working-capital up 142.7% (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11). Statutory tax rate rises 34% to 37% and Law 224/2025 cut incentives from 2026-04-01. Total active clients fell 3.3% y/y to 17.1m.
web_demand_product: Merchant acquiring plus embedded financial services. Merchants adopt PagBank POS/card acceptance, then its digital account: Q2 2026 Cash-In R$97.0bn (+23.3% y/y), deposits R$42.8bn (+15.1%), and credit R$5.1bn (+30.7%) - working capital, payroll loans, card receivables - plus merchant prepayment R$47.3bn. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_price_volume_mix: Mostly mix, some volume. Q2 2026 TPV grew 3.0% y/y (volume) yet Payments revenue fell 4.7% y/y (price/mix), while Banking revenue rose 28.9% y/y and reached 24% of revenue ex-ITC. Total revenue ex-ITC +1.7% y/y. Growth is Banking-mix-driven, not acquiring pricing power. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_bottleneck: Two: funding cost and credit underwriting. Q2 2026 financial costs were R$1,274m, 37.7% of revenue ex-ITC, tied to SELIC (14.54%). The company is scaling credit governance/analytics to underwrite unsecured SMB loans. The bottleneck it relieves for merchants is access to working capital and fast receivables liquidity. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_who_benefits_next: Second and third order: Brazil SMB merchants (prepayment, working capital), card networks and acquirer partners, depositors earning CDI-linked yields, and shareholders via buyback/dividends. Third-order: SME suppliers and marketplaces that get faster merchant cash conversion; consumers gaining cheaper digital accounts. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-01)
web_who_loses: Incumbent Brazilian banks and acquirers: Itau, Bradesco, Santander, Cielo, GetNet, Stone and consumer-finance lenders lose merchant/deposit share to PagBank lower-cost digital accounts and cheaper acquired funding. Internally, PagBank Payments segment loses mix share to its own Banking arm (Payments revenue -4.7% y/y). (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_margin_collapse_risk: Rising unsecured credit losses: Q2 2026 allowances R$70m vs R$28m and NPL90 3.4% vs 2.5%; higher SELIC/funding (financial costs R$1,274m); tax: statutory rate 34% to 37% and Law 224/2025 incentive cut from 2026-04-01; elevated marketing (World Cup sponsorship) and admin expenses. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_low_cost_substitute: Not Chinese; the closest low-cost substitute is Brazil Pix, free instant payments that undercut card MDR, plus Nubank, Mercado Pago, Stone and Cielo. PagBank itself pushes Pix/cash-in, R$97.0bn up 23.3% y/y, so the substitute is already at scale. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11)
web_ceo_promised: CEO Carlos Mauad, 2026-08-11: 2029 ambition is a R$25 billion Credit Portfolio, gross profit CAGR of approximately 10% and EPS CAGR above 16% between 2025 and 2029. On 2026-09-01 the company said it expects to distribute at least R$2.0bn dividends in 2027-2028 and a US$150m buyback. (SEC 6-K)
web_did_they_deliver: Partly. 2026-08-11 6-K: third US$200m buyback fully completed; over 19m shares/R$1bn repurchased in 12 months; US$0.26 special dividend paid June 2026; about R$600m of R$1.4bn 2026 dividends distributed. Credit portfolio only R$5.1bn versus the R$25bn 2029 goal; 6M2026 ex-ITC gross margin slipped to 57.9% from 59.1%.
web_what_would_falsify: Observables: NPL90 above about 4% of the credit portfolio, or quarterly credit-loss allowances staying above R$70m while unsecured share rises; BIS ratio falling below the 18% floor (22.5% in Q2 2026); the remaining about R$400m 2026 dividend and the US$0.28 due 2026-09-30 not paid; TPV turning negative y/y. (SEC 6-K 2026-08-11 and 2026-09-01)
